A1.justification: Both PDFs describe HairWeaver, and all supplied pages are readable. The method, equations, retained experiments, and supplementary material can be matched, distinguishing relocated content from material omitted in v2.

before.justification: V1 reports original CG and NeRSemble evaluations, component ablations, generated examples, and user studies, including the larger study in Section 7.2.

after.justification: V2 retains original benchmark and user-study results and adds Wan-VACE comparisons, a conditioning ablation, and qualitative examples.

M1.justification: The pose encoder, concatenated hair tokens, two-stage training, losses, and inference procedure remain unchanged. Style-Alignment-LoRA renames Sim2Real-Domain-LoRA. NeRSemble adaptation and Flux reference-image preprocessing were already documented in v1 Sections 9 and 8.

E1.justification: The CG and NeRSemble benchmarks remain, while Figure 6 adds an in-the-wild photographic-reference example beyond the controlled captures and generated references. TikTok training is no longer documented, but its omission does not establish that the underlying training corpus changed.

E2.justification: Tables 1 and 3 add fine-tuned Wan-VACE with matching hair/body conditions as a comparator. The existing five baselines remain, and comparator membership in the NeRSemble and retained user-study tables is unchanged.

E3.justification: New CG experiments evaluate Wan-VACE under matched conditioning and replace HairWeaver's UVW/normal inputs with alpha-map/DensePose inputs. V1's additional 45-participant, 20-video study is no longer reported. Existing benchmark sizes, metrics, and main training budgets remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Table 3 adds a coarse-versus-detailed conditioning ablation and a matched-condition Wan-VACE comparison addressing whether gains come from architecture or richer inputs. Figures 6–7 add photographic-reference and comparative case studies. Existing component ablations remain.

E5.justification: V2 removes the statistical-validation section and Table 7: the omnibus chi-square test, pairwise tests, significance reporting, and Cramér's V are absent. Only aggregate preference percentages remain, substantially reducing statistical reporting; neither version reports benchmark seed variation.

E6.justification: Retained numerical rows in Tables 1–4 are unchanged. V2 adds Wan-VACE and alpha-conditioned HairWeaver results, including hair PSNR values of 34.6198 and 36.7297, respectively. However, it removes subject-wise preferences, pairwise statistics, and the larger study reporting 68.17% preference for HairWeaver, substantially changing the supporting empirical record.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions and Equations 1–9 retain the same diffusion formulation, conditioning operations, objectives, and inference expression. No theoretical assumptions, propositions, or proofs are added or removed.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the claims of controllable photorealistic hair animation through synthetic training and two LoRA components. Replacing 'Few-Shot' with 'Physics Transfer' in the title shifts emphasis; the introduction still claims training with around 1,000 videos, and physics transfer was already central to v1.

C2.justification: V2 adds interpretations about architectural benefits under matched conditioning, retained physical priors with coarse inputs, reference-image realism, and downstream synthetic-data applications. Existing limitations remain. Its broad alpha-map superiority claim needs qualification: Table 3 reports hair SSIM 0.9693, below UniAnimate-DiT's 0.9761.

D1.justification: V2 omits v1 Section 9's TikTok-plus-CG training recipe and condition-extraction instructions, substantially reducing NeRSemble reproducibility information. Prolific recruitment details also disappear. V2 clarifies LoRA fine-tuning and supplies video-file locations, while the Flux/Euler inference recipe moves intact into Section 4.3.

R1.justification: V2 adds the VACE reference and positioning against conditioned video-to-video translation. The TikTok/Jafarian–Park and chi-square/McHugh references disappear with their supplementary discussions. The main related-work treatment, including ControlHair, is otherwise retained.

P1.justification: Most prose and the main narrative remain intact. V2 revises the title and LoRA terminology, moves photoreal inference into Section 4.3, omits two supplementary sections, and adds application discussion and acknowledgements. These are localized editorial and structural changes.

P2.justification: V2 adopts a substantially narrower conference layout with running headers, resized displays, and text wrapping around figures and tables. It replaces Figure 1, adds Figures 6–7, expands Tables 1 and 3, and removes Tables 5–7. These changes substantially alter visual presentation.

improvement.justification: The matched-condition Wan-VACE comparison and conditioning ablation improve the relevance of the supporting evidence. However, v2 removes the larger user study, detailed preference/statistical reporting, and the NeRSemble training recipe, reducing corroboration and reproducibility. Its new alpha-map interpretation also overgeneralizes the tabulated results. These material gains and losses do not establish a reliable net improvement or deterioration.
